exact_scalar_firewall_lemmas.statement: For N=pq with distinct primes, if s=0 mod p and s!=0 mod q, then gcd(s,N)=p; symmetrically for q.
For a nontrivial idempotent e mod pq, its CRT value is (0,1) or (1,0); hence gcd(e,N) and gcd(e-1,N) are the complementary prime factors.
For gamma^2=1 mod pq with gamma!=+/-1 mod pq, the hidden signs are opposite and gcd(gamma-1,N), gcd(gamma+1,N) give the complementary factors.

terminal_boundary.strongest_antecedent: Algebraic-group order/smoothness methods, especially ECM, already realize public N-only one-sided hidden-channel collapse through stateful nonunit emergence, but are explicitly excluded.
terminal_boundary.important_refinement: Classical stateful factoring often keeps each update map CRT-natural. What breaks the parent fixed finite grammar is process-level stopping/history/support growth, not necessarily ring-product naturality of an individual update.
terminal_boundary.surviving_residue: A candidate must be public-N-only and factor-blind; non-fixed-term/stateful; pre-collapse scalar-gcd clean; and not reducible to group-order smoothness, collision, congruence-of-squares/relation, named-prime p-adic, or direct nonunit/idempotent/root extraction.
